design_rationale:
STEP 0 SNAPSHOT (task 1 of 2, claimed second, final task -- closes difficulty-wide coverage): task 0 already claimed corp_ext_dues_billing, corp_ext_payment_allocation, corp_ext_wellness_reimbursement_waiver, the difficulty's single workflow (corp_wf_new_enrollment_onboarding), and tools activate_corp_enrollment_8f54bf3c / bill_corp_enrollment_dues_4e718c02 / record_corp_dues_payment_5148c010 / waive_corp_wellness_reimbursement_b40ef430. This task claims the remaining headroom: corp_billing_and_suspension's late-fee/suspension machinery and reinstatement, via 3 new extended policies (corp_ext_late_fee_assessment, corp_ext_missed_payment_recovery, corp_ext_reinstatement_billing) and 3 new tools, all pairwise disjoint from task 0's scope. Together, task 0 and task 1 cover every extended_policy this difficulty declares.

ROUND 2 REVISION (per source-layer audit SOURCE-TASK RED on this task): corp_ext_late_fee_assessment's target tool bill_corp_late_fee_4428c2eb takes a billing_cycle_month argument that the policy's rule/compute_basis/compute never bound, so with 2 missed cycles the gold '2026-08' and an equally-defensible '2026-07' were two solutions. Fixed by adding a rule sentence pinning the combined late fee to 'the enrollment's most recently billed cycle' and a compute binding billing_cycle_month_value=LATEST('corporate_wellness_events','billing_cycle_month', date_field='event_timestamp', event_type='corp_dues_billed') that deterministically resolves to '2026-08' (the latest of the 5 corp_dues_billed rows by event_timestamp) in this task's world; this task's own evaluation_criteria argument_uniqueness_tracing for billing_cycle_month now quotes that rule sentence and binding instead of an author-supplied 'most recent unpaid cycle' convention.

ROUND 3 REVISION (per policy_kb/runtime_context rework: KB-RUNTIME RED / KB-BIJECTION RED): corp_ext_late_fee_assessment's surcharge and corp_ext_missed_payment_recovery's ceiling both read cross-category CPARAM('membership','late_fee_usd'/'monthly_dues_usd') -- club-membership-tier catalogue parameters with no exposed tool field and, for this task's seed as originally authored, no observable ledger fact either (Marcus's own membership_events was empty), so GT's $103.00/$147.00 could not be derived from the runtime-visible KB+DB alone (a blind derivation landed at $100.00/$144.00, assuming a $0.00 surcharge for lack of any observable rate). Fixed per option (a): seeded 3 new membership_events rows on Marcus's own Premier All-Access membership (a $64.99 recurring_dues charge, its $64.99 payment, and a $15.00 late_fee charge, reconciling exactly to the existing dues_balance=15.00) so both catalogue values are now independently observable as real ledger facts -- exactly the mechanism that already made task 0 solvable. Added a find_membership_events read step (now evaluation_criteria step 5) so the agent's read path actually surfaces these rows, and updated both policies' rule text (corp.extended.yaml) to state this resolution mechanism explicitly, closing the difficulty-wide KB-bijection documentation gap as well as the runtime miss. No GT dollar amount changed for this task (late fee remains $103.00, recovery payment remains $147.00, reinstatement fee remains $25.00) -- only the world's observability of the pre-existing catalogue values changed.

WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST: the caller's surface goal ('reactivate my enrollment, HR says the payment issue is sorted') never names a late fee, a missed-payment amount or a reinstatement fee; the agent must read corp_billing_and_suspension to discover a late fee is owed at all, reconcile the enrollment's own billing history (5 billed, 3 paid) to size both the late fee and the payment, and read corp_ext_reinstatement_billing to discover the fee is conditionally waived by the employee's own club membership standing and further halved by household add-on membership -- none of which the caller states or hints. Difficulty is long (late fee -> payment -> reinstatement, 3 non-swappable steps) and broad (a per-cycle floor plus a cross-category membership-late-fee surcharge, a two-history-column reconciliation (billed vs paid) to size missed_cycles, a cross-category payment ceiling, and two independent cross-category checks -- membership dues_balance and household add-on existence -- deciding the reinstatement fee).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD: corp_billing_and_suspension / corp_tier_pricing govern corp_dues_billed (both policy_scope, no structured eligibility) and are satisfied trivially since the enrollment already exists and is open (suspended, not closed). corp_dues_waiver_policy's own structured eligibility (waiver_requires_open_enrollment) applies_to=[corp_dues_waived] only, not corp_dues_payment_received, so the payment step carries it only as policy_scope. No time-kind eligibility governs any of this task's writes (corp_re_enrollment_cooldown only governs corp_enrollment_created, which this task never writes).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: the target object is Marcus's own corporate wellness enrollment (enrollment_id=dc09a6e0-ac3a-45ea-bfe9-82b7c7fc7361), customer_id=1105808c-2bda-4f14-9ddd-05aa48cb4e22, employer_account_id=EMP-2209-ST. Its 8 seeded billing-history rows are the exact SUM/COUNT scope for every computation here (auto-scoped to enrollment_id=HID); no other employee's history could ever leak in. The 5 billed / 3 paid split is deliberately unbalanced by exactly suspension_after_missed_payments=2 for Startup Partner, so the seed is internally consistent with why this enrollment is suspended in the first place.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root_problem = corp_ext_reinstatement_billing (the caller's surface ask: 'get my enrollment reactivated'). Edge 1: reinstatement -> corp_ext_missed_payment_recovery, kind=state_gate, gate=corporate_wellness_enrollments.corporate_dues_balance. Condition/policy_source (quoted from corp_ext_reinstatement_billing's own rule): 'A reinstatement fee may only be billed once the employer's master account no longer shows any outstanding missed-payment balance for this enrollment.' Unresolved at frozen_time because corporate_dues_balance=44.00 (positive) at initial_state.corporate_wellness_enrollments.dc09a6e0-ac3a-45ea-bfe9-82b7c7fc7361.corporate_dues_balance. Resolved by post_corp_dues_payment_af691ae5; once that lands, corporate_dues_balance flips to 0.00. Edge 2: missed_payment_recovery -> corp_ext_late_fee_assessment, kind=value_input, gate=current_balance. Condition/policy_source (quoted from corp_ext_missed_payment_recovery's own rule): 'A payment intended to bring the employer's master account current must be posted only once every currently due charge, including any outstanding late-payment fee, has been billed against the enrollment.' Unresolved at frozen_time because the late fee itself has not yet been billed (only the 5 regular recurring charges exist in initial_state; no late-fee row exists yet). Resolved by bill_corp_late_fee_4428c2eb; once that lands, current_balance rises from 44.00 to 147.00. Topological order: corp_ext_late_fee_assessment -> corp_ext_missed_payment_recovery -> corp_ext_reinstatement_billing -- a strict total order, since missed_payment_recovery is itself a prerequisite of the root AND is itself downstream of late_fee_assessment. DELETION SENSITIVITY: skipping the late fee leaves current_balance at 44.00 (was 147.00) so missed_payment_recovery's own amount_usd becomes 44.00 (unpaid-late-fee scenario) instead of 147.00, and corporate_dues_balance would still show a residual gap after that smaller payment if the caller's own tendered figure were fixed -- but more directly, skipping the payment leaves corporate_dues_balance at a positive value (147.00) so the reinstatement's own state_gate remains false and no correct agent would bill the reinstatement fee at all -- both edges are load-bearing. user_scenario never names a late fee, a missed cycle, a payment amount or a reinstatement fee; the caller only ever expresses the single surface goal of getting the enrollment reactivated. The tool layer validates nothing: bill_corp_late_fee_4428c2eb, post_corp_dues_payment_af691ae5 and bill_corp_reinstatement_fee_377eb087 (which also flips status to active) each simply write their given amount_usd with no precondition check in task_tools.py (each only checks that the enrollment_id row exists).

STANDARD SOLUTION / STEP 5 VERIFICATION: locate Marcus via find_customers, verify identity (phone_number + photo_id_last4, 2 matches), find his suspended enrollment (dc09a6e0-ac3a-45ea-bfe9-82b7c7fc7361, corporate_dues_balance=44.00), read its full billing history (5 corp_dues_billed, 3 corp_dues_payment_received), read his own membership holding (Premier All-Access, monthly_dues_usd=64.99, late_fee_usd=15.00, dues_balance=15.00), and confirm he holds no active household add-on. Bill the late fee: corp_late_fee=P('late_payment_fee_usd')=50.00, membership_late_fee=CPARAM('membership','late_fee_usd')=15.00, surcharge=RND(0.10*15.00,2)=1.50, per_cycle_fee=RND(50.00+1.50,2)=51.50, billed_count=5, paid_count=3, missed_cycles=2 (the 'floor at 0' branch does NOT bind -- untriggered), result=RND(51.50*2,2)=103.00. Post the payment: current_balance=F('corporate_dues_balance')=44.00+103.00=147.00, membership_dues=CPARAM('membership','monthly_dues_usd')=64.99, ceiling=50*64.99=3249.50 (does not bind -- untriggered), floored_balance=147.00, amount_applied=147.00, result=147.00; balance -> 0.00. Bill the reinstatement fee (and reinstate): membership_balance=CFIELD('membership','dues_balance')=15.00 (>0, so the waiver branch does NOT bind -- untriggered), base_fee=P('reinstatement_fee_usd')=25.00, fee_after_membership_check=25.00, has_addon=EXISTS('addon',status='active')=False (untriggered), fee_component=25.00*1=25.00, result=25.00. This was executed with the actual compute expressions above and matches computations[].expected exactly.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT ONLY (masking compute/expected/GT): reading only the published rule prose, the tool docstrings, and the caller's own words, a rollout would (1) locate and verify the caller, (2) find his suspended enrollment and its full billing history, (3) discover from corp_ext_late_fee_assessment's rendered rule that a late fee (with a membership-linked surcharge) is owed on every currently unpaid cycle and compute it from the billed/paid history, (4) discover from corp_ext_missed_payment_recovery's rendered rule that a reinstatement payment must first clear the late fee together with the underlying arrears, (5) discover from corp_ext_reinstatement_billing's rendered rule that the reinstatement fee is conditionally waived and halved by cross-category facts, and read the employee's own membership and household add-on holdings to resolve them. This converges on the identical write sequence, objects and parameters as gold above with no second reasonable reading.
user_scenario: Marcus Whitfield calls in sounding relieved to finally get this handled. "Hi, this is Marcus Whitfield -- My corporate wellness enrollment through Ridgeline Manufacturing got suspended a little while back, and HR just told me the billing mix-up on their end is sorted out now, so I was hoping you could get my enrollment reactivated today." If asked how to verify him, he gives his phone number, "2125550430", and if a second detail is needed he mentions his driver license number is "DL-W4056789", of which the last four digits are "6789". If asked whether he wants the representative handling this for him, he says he'd really appreciate it if the representative could just take care of it for him. He mentions in passing that he's not calling about his regular club membership today, that's all fine -- he is only calling about the corporate enrollment. He does not know anything about how a late fee or a reinstatement charge is calculated, and does not bring either up; he is just repeating that HR said the payment issue is resolved on the employer side. If the representative explains that a few things need to be brought current before the enrollment can be reactivated, he says that is fine, go ahead and handle whatever needs handling. Once the representative tells him the enrollment is active again, he thanks them and says that's all he needed, thanks so much.
